findings.reason: an implementer following the closing sentence stores the geometry in the source-keyed plant cache, which by §6's own justification cannot serve a new source, so check 2's new-source calls would still rebuild and the fix would fail its own measure.
findings.text: §6's compatibility paragraph says of the pinned plant entry "the geometry is stored beside the plant rather than in place of it", but check 1 (§189) states "The geometry belongs in the sectioned-set cache, because a source-keyed entry cannot serve a source it has never seen"; the two sentences place the geometry in different caches

(snapshot §6) — §6 requires that "any plasma source drives the full ITER plant without rebuilding the sectioned set", but `coupled_plant(machine, source)` takes the sectioned machine as an argument and loads no sectioned-set cache itself (`nova/circuit/coupled_plant.py:164`), and the only caller that today obtains the refined geometry rebuilds it in-process via `subdivide_passive_thickness` (`scripts/iter_vessel_evolution/evolve.py:88` `conductor_geometry`), not through the cache — §6 names the reader `load_circuit_system` but no production caller that must be changed to read the geometry from the cache; WOULD_CHANGE_THE_PLAN: yes — REASON: without naming that caller the node can land the geometry in the cache while every source still rebuilds the sectioned set in the consumer, leaving check 2's zero-build counter red and the mechanism reached by no production path.
